analysis: The code iterates over a Set<String> validRedirects and for each validRedirect, it first adds the original string to a new HashSet<String> resolveValidRedirects. Then it checks if the string starts with '/' and if so, converts it to an absolute URI and adds the result again. The add method is from HashSet which implements Set. According to the javadoc, add can throw UnsupportedOperationException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, and IllegalArgumentException. Since HashSet supports the add operation, UnsupportedOperationException is avoided. The element type is String, which is compatible with HashSet<String>, so ClassCastException is avoided. IllegalArgumentException is avoided because Strings generally have no property preventing addition to a HashSet. NullPointerException may occur if validRedirect is null. The code does not perform any null check before the first add call; if validRedirect is null, the first add will throw NullPointerException. The second add inside the if block also could throw NullPointerException if validRedirect is null, but the preceding startsWith call would also throw NullPointerException first. Therefore, NullPointerException is not avoided because the input set may contain null elements.
answer: UnsupportedOperationException: avoided; ClassCastException: avoided; NullPointerException: not avoided; IllegalArgumentException: avoided.
remark: The NullPointerException can be triggered if the validRedirects set contains a null element. The first call to resolveValidRedirects.add(validRedirect) will throw NullPointerException because HashSet.add(null) throws NullPointerException when the set does not allow null elements (which is the default for HashSet). The code does not perform any null check on the input elements, so this exception is not avoided.
